claims.event: Commanded at Dengzhou and Luoyang, was acting councilor at Xuzhou, executed Master Li, and was captured and killed fleeing through the mountains in Tianxing 1.
As overall commander of Guan-Shaan he evacuated Shaanzhou and later gathered nearly ten thousand returning fugitives.
Relayed the imperial order summoning Wudian to reinforce the capital.
Tong Pass commander who marched with Wudian and was captured and executed with him.
Qin-Lan commander who surrendered first and was beheaded by the Mongols.
Commandant of Anping who joined Wudian's relief army.
Commandant of Bandit-Suppression who joined Wudian's relief army.
Commandant of Zhenwu whose force defected toward Zhuyang and surrendered to the Mongols.
Sent with eighty grain boats to Lingbao, where he surrendered to the Mongols.
Volunteer leader who built a water barrier at Lingbao and was overrun by the Mongols.
Volunteer leader who with Zhang Xin defended a water barrier at Lingbao and was overrun.
Mongol general who failed to break the Lingbao barrier until Suoye's boats surrendered.
Shaanzhou vice prefect who volunteered for the campaign and recruited eight hundred men.
Raised the Enemy-Breaking Army in under two days and was made acting military commissioner of the Xingbao Army.
Pacification commissioner of Tong and Hua who repeatedly dissuaded Wudian from treachery and plunder.
Sortied without orders at Shaanzhou and was nearly captured when his horse stumbled.
Advised Wudian to seize Weizhou and was executed for leaking military secrets.
Killed Miao Ying for refusing to surrender and took his head to the Mongols.
Refused Zheng Tong's demand to surrender and was killed.
Hereditary mouke on close terms with Wudian, which led the army to march toward Deng.

label.en: Military Commissioner of the Wusheng Army
Pacification Commissioner of Tong and Hua
Acting Military Commissioner of the Xingbao Army

claims.event: In the fifth month led troops to re-establish the Shangzhou overall command.
Established a hold at Guo Prefecture and served as acting prefect.
Appointed overall commander of Guan-Shaan and acting councilor, then killed in Zhao Wei's night attack on Shaanzhou.
Entered Shaanzhou as councilor of state and was later summoned to Liushan Temple in Nanyang.
Zhenyou 3 jinshi who re-established mountain stockades and was cruelly killed by Zhao Wei, who resented him.
Starved of rations, he massacred the Shaanzhou provincial staff, was appointed left army supervising general, then surrendered to the Mongols.
Sent by the provincial headquarters as acting commander to hold Yongning's Yuanjia stockade.
Infiltrated Shaanzhou with thirty men and opened the way for Zhao Wei's troops.
Commander killed in Zhao Wei's attack on Shaanzhou.
Overall chief killed in Zhao Wei's attack on Shaanzhou.
Refused to follow the rebel Zhao Wei and drowned himself in the river.
Summoned to reinforce the capital; after defeat west of Zheng rode alone to the capital and reported Wudian's defeat.
Denounced as chief culprit of the Tieling defeat; his property was confiscated.
Property confiscated after the Tieling defeat.
Property confiscated after the Tieling defeat.
In Xingding 3 appointed right deputy commander at Pingliang and proposed fortifying Zhenrong against the Tanguts.
Urged replacing the mediocre Nüxilie Gulijian at Pingliang.
Criticized by Xu Ding as a mediocre commander who bought his rank with grain.

label.en: Assistant Commissioner of the Left and Right Departments

claims.event: Proposed garrison farming, became military commissioner of the Changwu Army, defended Guide in Zhengda 9 and was made overall commander with the golden tiger tally.
Led armies from Zhending, Xin'an, Daming, Dongping and Yidu against Guide.
His routed troops arrived at Guide and lifted the defenders' morale.
Recruited by Nülühuan as commander and led a night raid on the Mongol camp at Guide.
Said to have buried the ancient cannon found at Guide; besieged at Suiyang by Yin Ziqi.
His general Yin Ziqi captured Suiyang.
Attacked Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan and captured Suiyang.
Defended Suiyang with Zhang Xun against Yin Ziqi.
Defended Guide with all his strength during the Mongol siege.
Defended Guide with all his strength during the Mongol siege.
Defended Guide with all his strength during the Mongol siege.
Defended Guide with all his strength during the Mongol siege.
Sent to breach the Phoenix Pool dam and seized by Mongol scouts.
Made military commissioner of the Jiqing Army when the Directorate of Agriculture was abolished.
Appointed vice prefect of Guide Prefecture.
Appointed prefectural judge of Guide.

label.en: Military Commissioner of the Changwu Army
Military Commissioner of the Jiqing Army

claims.event: Halted at Huangling Hill in Tianxing 1 and sent officers to Guide to levy grain.
Sent by Aizong to Guide to levy grain.
Sent by Aizong to Guide to levy grain.
Sent by Nülühuan to escort 1,500 shi of grain to the emperor.
Escorted grain to the emperor as acting bureau director.
Escorted grain to the emperor as acting commander.
Seized and killed by Guannu at Guide for withholding supplies; later his office was restored.
Held Guide with nearly seven hundred men and was killed when Guannu attacked his army.
His army had once been suppressed by Ma Yong, a man of the same district.
Escaped captivity, rose to command the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army, and mutinied at Guide, killing Ma Yong and Nülühuan.
Entered Cai and petitioned for the vindication of his uncle Nülühuan.
His biography records the vindication of Nülühuan.
Replaced Nülühuan as overall commander and was killed by two soldiers Guannu sent.
Commanded the routed Hebei troops and beheaded four grumblers, throwing the armies into uproar.
His household was robbed by mutinous troops at Guide.
His household was robbed by mutinous troops at Guide.
Attacked Pingyang, where Guannu ranked first in merit.
Sent by Guannu to persuade Nihe, but revealed the truth to him.
Deng commander who planned to capture Guannu in the jar-city fortification.
Bound by Guannu and falsely presented as prefect of Tangzhou.
Led the generals in battle at Huangling Hill.

label.en: Commander of Ten Thousand of the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army

claims.event: Plotted with Guo Yong'an, attacked Ma Yong, massacred court officials, was made deputy commissioner of military affairs and negotiated secretly with Temü.
Held Guide with seven hundred men and was routed by Guannu after the reconciliation banquet.
Attacked Guide and returned Guannu's mother to settle a peace plan.
Plotted with Guannu to take the emperor to Haizhou and returned with a memorial.
Sent Guo Yong'an back with a memorial urging the emperor to go to Haizhou.
Blocked the proposal to cross north and was killed by Guannu at his home.
Warned the emperor of Guannu's rebellion and was killed with over three hundred officials.
Warned the emperor that Guannu showed signs of rebellion.
Warned the emperor that Guannu showed signs of rebellion.
Ordered to watch Guannu, he leaked the emperor's intentions and was sent to negotiate with Temü.
Ordered to watch Guannu covertly, he leaked the emperor's intentions instead.
Court officials seized by Guannu were held under guard at his residence.
Sent to seize Banushen before the emperor but withdrew without pressing.
The emperor asked that he be left to attend him when Ma Shi came to seize him.
Drowned himself during Guannu's mutiny.
Zhi'ning 1 jinshi from Longshan who planned Guide's defense and was killed in the mutiny after refusing to flee.
Captured by northern troops, returned by Temü, and offered by Guannu as a hostage.
Surrounded Guannu's residence and made him promise to kill northern envoys.

claims.event: Led the fire-lance night attack at Wangjia Temple, was made councilor and left deputy commander, then was stabbed by Wanchu and killed.
Withdrew after Guannu promised to stop speaking of peace.
Left by Guannu in command of his army when Guannu entered Bozhou.
Plotted with the emperor to kill Guannu and was made a military commissioner.
Pursued and killed the wounded Guannu and was made a military commissioner.
Pursued and killed the wounded Guannu and was made a military commissioner.
Lay in ambush at Zhaobi Hall, stabbed Guannu in the ribs and was made right guard general.
Reportedly ordered by Guannu to plot with Guo Yong'an to coerce the emperor.
Reportedly involved in Guannu's scheme to force the emperor to abdicate.
Ordered to summon the chief ministers on the day Guannu was killed.
Given the tiger tally and sent to reassure the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army.
Summoned after Guannu's death and made commander of the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army.
Summoned after Guannu's death and made commander of the Loyalty-and-Filiality Army.
Summoned after Guannu's death, arrived first and was killed below the hall.
Realized the plot midway and was killed by stray arrows.
Alone excluded from the emperor's amnesty.
Chief inspector whom Guannu once followed through Cai.
Sent to Cai and reported that its walls, troops and grain were inadequate.
Granted monthly grain by imperial order after Guannu's death.

claims.event: Robbed the treasury, was jailed, escaped during the mutiny killing three officials, and was beheaded at Bozhou.
His mutiny let Xi Xian escape; he was later executed.
Interrogated Xi Xian and was killed at home by him.
Interrogated Xi Xian and was killed at home by him.
Killed by Xi Xian at the palace gate.
Ordered to behead Xi Xian and Loyalty-and-Filiality leaders at Bozhou.
Killed on the road by Wure.
Waited on the road and killed Guo Yong'an.
Son of Guaishan; defended Xuyi and lost badly, was captured at Yangyi Post and killed for refusing to surrender.
Overall military commissioner and father of Wanyan Chengli.
Chief minister and cousin of Chengli, who sent him letters seeking recall.
Welcomed by Qingshannu at Terrace City and appointed him deputy defender of the Western Capital.
Monopolized power and was later executed.
Sent against Xia at Tongqin Fort and defeated them.
Held Chuzhou and crushed the Jin army at the Xuyi border.
Defended Xuyi with Qingshannu.
Memorialized asking to behead Qingshannu.
Left to defend Jingzhao when Qingshannu withdrew.
Refused Qingshannu an audience and sent him to Huangling Hill.
Sent by Aizong to give Qingshannu authority at Huangling Hill.
Replaced by Qingshannu at Xuzhou.
Commanded elite troops with Qingshannu and died in battle; nephew of Saibu.
Surrendered to the Mongols with Yisheng Army troops.
Surrendered to the Mongols with Yisheng Army troops.
Surrendered to the Mongols with Yisheng Army troops.
Fled to Guide after the rout.
Fled to Guide after the rout.
Zhending commander who met the captive Chengli.
Tried to make Chengli induce the capital to surrender.
Abandoned Suizhou, fled to Guide and died at Yangyi Post.
Chief minister whose position kept his nephew Ulun in command.
